Save a table, figure or report

Source: R/report.R
jp_save.Rd

Writes a result table, a figure or an interactive graphic to a file whose format follows its extension, for a manuscript, a report or a presentation.

Usage

jp_save(
  x,
  file,
  title = NULL,
  note = NULL,
  digits = 3,
  width = 7.5,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300,
  label = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A data frame, a ggplot, an htmlwidget or a joinpoint fit.

file

Output file; the extension sets the format.

title

Optional caption of the table or figure.

note

Optional note printed under the table or figure.

digits

Decimals of the numeric columns of a table (character columns, such as those of jp_table(), are written as they are). In .csv, .tsv and .txt files numbers stay numeric (p values rounded to digits significant digits); other formats show p values with three decimals, and below 0.001 as "< 0.001". Line breaks inside cells of Markdown and document tables become spaces.

width, height, dpi

Size of a figure in inches and its resolution.

label

Optional LaTeX label (.tex output).

...

Further arguments to jp_report() when x is a fit.

Value

The path of the written file, invisibly.

Details

  • Tables (data frames such as the results of jp_table(), apc() or model_selection()$criteria): .csv, .tsv, .txt, .md (Markdown pipe table), .tex (LaTeX table with booktabs rules; load \usepackage{booktabs}), .html, .docx (Word table), .odt, .rtf, .pptx and .pdf.

  • Figures (ggplot objects such as autoplot() or plot_apc()): the image formats of ggplot2::ggsave() (.png, .pdf, .svg, .jpeg, .tiff, .eps, ...), .tex (a LaTeX figure that includes a PDF of the figure written beside it), and .html, .docx, .odt, .rtf, .pptx and .md documents holding the figure.

  • Interactive graphics (jp_interactive()): .html, a standalone web page (without Pandoc, a page with its scripts in the folder <name>_files beside it).

  • A joinpoint fit: a complete report, see jp_report().

Word, OpenDocument, PowerPoint, RTF, HTML and PDF documents are made with Pandoc, which comes with RStudio and Quarto (or see https://pandoc.org), through the rmarkdown package; PDF documents also need LaTeX (for example tinytex::install_tinytex()).

Examples

tb <- subset(us_mortality, cause == "Tuberculosis")
fit <- joinpoint(tb, year, rate, kmax = 2, ci_method = "parametric")
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "joinpoint-save")
dir.create(dir)
jp_save(jp_table(fit), file.path(dir, "trends.tex"),
        title = "Trends in tuberculosis mortality")
jp_save(jp_table(fit), file.path(dir, "trends.md"))
jp_save(autoplot(fit), file.path(dir, "trend.png"), width = 6, height = 4)
if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) &&
    rmarkdown::pandoc_available()) {
  jp_save(jp_table(fit), file.path(dir, "trends.docx"))
}
list.files(dir)
#> [1] "trend.png"   "trends.docx" "trends.md"   "trends.tex" 
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
